title.narrative: Strengthening Rule of Law, Access to Justice pathways to accelerate India’s Sustainable Development

description.narrative: UNDP’s global programming on rule of law promotion and people centered access to justice is widely recognised for its ability to provide technical and strategic expertise, mobilise funds and collaborate and coordinate across UN entities to enable more holistic, coherent, and comprehensive responses to challenges on the subject. This includes adoption of a cross disciplinary approach for promoting the mandate to achieve sustainable development by transforming systems to be more inclusive, people-centered and capacitated thereby making them more trusted and accessible, ensuring more people have access to justice and redress; advancing gender equality and women’s advancement, and most significantly ensuring that the development perspective infuses rule of law and access to justice interventions. To leverage these strengths and to build on UNDP’s past expansive programming on access to justice in India (2008-2017), Business and Human Rights centric interventions (2020-till date) and its recent re-engagement with NALSA and DOJ at the RLAC on Access to Legal Aid, UNDP proposes to re-initiate programming on strengthening rule of law and access to justice pathways in India. The project aims to address structural and root challenges that hinder meaningful access to justice for those furthest behind (LNOB lens) by identifying actions and interventions to address these gaps. While acknowledging ‘digitization’ of legal and justice services as an enabler for accessing justice effectively, meaningfully and in a timely way by all, the project aims to also highlight the need for non-technology led innovative solutions (people centered and community led solutions) considering the specificities of varied contexts. Role of both formal and informal justice processes, including alternate dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms will be explored in meeting people’s need for quality justice solutions.
